abstract: A low energy fusion pathway must coordinate access to a reacting state, the source of control work, nuclear product formation, and restoration of its mediator. This paper assimilates eighteen core K-Field papers within a twenty-five-artifact source inventory, including the current continuum, capture, antipodal-network, curvature, Mass Bridge, interference, and multiport results together with earlier rotating-mass and photon-energy coupling work. It derives a composite candidate in which an advancing Earth-referenced field phase supplies reciprocal work, differential and pair-compatible couplings register the incoming state, coordinated controls reduce internal state deformation, and a product-selective doorway completes the reaction. A fixed-phase two-state compensation identity is extended to complex controls and to a multichannel projection criterion. Fresh diagonalization of the archived neutron–proton E1 product matrix gives 93.36469 microbarn for its optimal eight-mode coherent state, compared with 19.13294 microbarn for the equal-flux incoherent mixture, a factor of 4.87979 in that partial channel at 100 keV. Explicit position averaging quantifies the dependence on local phase registration. A separate dimensionless model integrates ordered transfer, product release, mediator restoration, and phase-receiver work in one cycle: the stipulated product probability is 0.9999679, with conservation residuals below 8 × 10⁻¹⁵ in model units. The resulting pathway is established as a sufficient, internally consistent reduced mechanism under stated coupling assumptions. Its realization as low energy charged-particle fusion remains determined by the common microscopic receiving operator, charged entrance continuum, preparation cost, and product spectrum. The paper formulates those remaining quantities as a finite identification problem and provides reproducible calculations, predictions, source locators, and an audit correction record.

It does not establish a charged-fuel rate or useful net power from the current inputs. The remaining bridge is the shared microscopic operator connecting the calibrated optical/mechanical receiver to the charged entrance, mediator controls and nuclear product spectrum.

The most informative continuation is to resolve that operator’s nuclear-sensitive null directions and calculate the complete cycle at physical units. blocks.text: For a normalized two-state eigenvector, the Fubini–Study line element is one quarter of dθ² + sin²θ dφ². A fixed θ with changing physical azimuth therefore has nonzero tangent metric. A fixed eigenvector family has commuting traceless Hamiltonians; its changing eigenvalue still entails work when the Hamiltonian is externally varied.

For multiple excited channels, write A = diag(Δn⁻¹)Vu and b = diag(Δn⁻¹)vR, stacking real and imaginary parts. Minimizing ||b + Au′||² gives u′ = −A⁺b and residual (I − AA⁺)b. The equivalent Schur complement is gRR − gRu guu⁺ guR. Positivity ensures guR lies in the supported range; exact cancellation requires b in the range of A.

For inertia minimization, replace Δn⁻¹ by Δn raised to the power −3/2 and multiply the squared norm by 2ℏ². Exact cancellation is shared when all relevant gaps are finite, but incomplete minimizers may differ. blocks.text: For a normalized two-state eigenvector, the Fubini–Study line element is one quarter of dθ² + sin²θ dφ². A fixed θ with changing physical azimuth therefore has nonzero tangent metric. A fixed eigenvector family has commuting traceless Hamiltonians; its changing eigenvalue still entails work when the Hamiltonian is externally varied.

For multiple excited channels, write A = diag(Δn⁻¹)Vu and b = diag(Δn⁻¹)vR, stacking real and imaginary parts. Minimizing ||b + Au′||² gives u′ = −A⁺b and residual (I − AA⁺)b. The equivalent Schur complement is gRR − gRu guu⁺ guR. Positivity ensures guR lies in the supported range; exact cancellation requires b in the range of A.

For inertia minimization, replace Δn⁻¹ by Δn raised to the power −3/2 and multiply the squared norm by 2ℏ². Exact cancellation is shared when all relevant gaps are finite, but incomplete minimizers may differ. Path integrability, transverse confinement and bare actuator mass are additional conditions; the pointwise minimum does not supply them.

For a tangent with nonnegative weights an = |vn|², let S1 = Σan/Δn, S2 = Σan/Δn² and S3 = Σan/Δn³. Applying Cauchy–Schwarz to √(an/Δn) and √(an/Δn³) gives S2² ≤ S1S3. If one physically admissible Hamiltonian provides the receiving, relative-transfer, control, product and reset interfaces below, then a laboratory cycle can use externally supplied phase work to transfer an incoming state into an energy-releasing product while returning its mediator, without macroscopically occupying the high intermediate state.

The preferred composite uses receiving work to maintain a locally registered pair state, then a compensated approach or relay, followed by a matched nuclear exit and mediator return. Static dressing can assist the same route. These mechanisms can cooperate because they address different bottlenecks, but the combined evolution—not a product of separate gain factors—determines the result.

Physical catalysis already has a precise nuclear precedent in muon-assisted reactions: a mediator changes the route to nuclear contact. That comparison supports the question of reusable access; it does not calibrate K-Field matrix elements or establish their cost. [E9]

A pathway can have low bulk temperature yet still rely on a small energetic component. It can have low intermediate occupation yet require a costly phase preparation. It can transfer an already admitted state efficiently while leaving the low-energy entrance probability tiny. Consequently the physical figure of merit must include every stage, with their shared state correlations.

Here ηQ is the usable fraction of product release under a specified output system, not an assumed unit efficiency. Each power refers to a distinct port; any term already paid from PK must not be subtracted again elsewhere. Throughput depends on loading time, prepared-pair density, admission probability, passage duration, product release and mediator reuse. The dimensionless high-transfer cycle supplies no physical value for those rates.

A genuine low-incident-energy route must change the charged entrance dynamics or demonstrate a non-negligible admitted state at the chosen energy. Coherent phase selection alone cannot remove a common vanishing threshold factor from a finite matrix K(E) = f(E)K0 + higher-order terms. A coordinate relabeling likewise cannot change the physical action. A new relative interaction can change it, but that interaction must appear in the common Hamiltonian.

The archived collective calculation illustrates the importance of a complete comparison: an attractive contribution of −6.9072667 MeV coexists with a corrected barrier maximum of +0.95886672 MeV and an inertia factor 1.32642253. It is a separate 33-state construction from the exact capture model; its attraction cannot be combined with the E1 gain as if they were one calculation. [S08]

The foundation therefore supports a directed search for a low-action, low-control-cost, product-bright route. It does not select “low energy” by choosing whichever of these measures happens to improve in isolation.

Table 8 specifies discriminating comparisons and retained outcomes. A passive receiver need not reverse harvested power when traversal reverses. More discriminating comparisons separate the sign of imposed phase, physical chirality, traversal frequency, load and occupation. These controls distinguish the proposed coupling tensor from a scalar gain without discarding unexplained channels.

Failure of a prediction localizes the interface that needs revision. Conversely, correlated product and source-residue predictions from a shared operator would reduce the number of freely adjustable explanations.

A two-state path with delta*J_prime-J*delta_prime=0 keeps the eigenvector fixed while its energy can change.
The minimum tangent quantum metric is the control-space Schur complement; its residual identifies unavailable compensation.
An energy-matched three-state chain transfers 0.99811933 into a doorway with peak intermediate population 0.00010379 in the declared model.
The largest eigenvalue of the archived eight-mode pn E1 matrix is 93.36468877 microbarn, 4.87978714 times its equal-flux incoherent mean.
Desired nuclear coupling must survive projection onto the kernel of unwanted outputs and the reachable control span.
A Gaussian positional averaging example yields antipodal visibility exp(-2 k^2 sigma_x^2).
Matching doorway widths can give a unit peak while the integrated response retains the entrance-width bottleneck.
Lucas scale correspondence constrains a candidate interlevel channel but does not identify its off-diagonal coupling.
The unified candidate is a reusable phase-driven mediator joining local pair coherence, compensated approach and a matched nuclear exit.
The earlier chiral elastic coupling and photon-energy receiving map supply a two-function mediator candidate.
A nuclear projection is identifiable from calibrated response data only when it annihilates the measurement null space in the declared operator basis.
Projection of the common physical vertex distinguishes photon energy gradients from the relative nuclear channel and its mass-proportional cancellation.
